chunks: From him, from al-Haytham, from al-Nahdi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih al-Kazzaz, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'We bring goods from Sana'a and sell them in Mecca for ten, thirteen, or twelve [dirhams], and when we bring them, merchants from the merchants of Mecca come out to us and give us, in addition to that, eleven, ten and a half, or less. Should I sell them [there] or bring them to Mecca?' He said to me: 'Sell them on the road and do not bring them to Mecca, for indeed Allah the Exalted disliked that the trade of the believer be in Mecca.'

key_terms.صَنْعَاءَ: Sana'a, a city in Yemen known for trade

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling imported goods in Mecca according to Imam Musa al-Kazim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) advises selling goods from Sana'a on the road rather than bringing them into Mecca, citing that Allah disliked the believer's trade being concentrated there. This ruling highlights the principle of preventing market dominance or 'monopoly' (Ihtikar) by local merchants in the holy city, ensuring fair competition and preventing the exploitation of pilgrims. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on economic justice and the spiritual sanctity of trade practices in sacred spaces.
